DATED  
 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE  FIR/ORDER) NO. 25066 of 2017  ==========================================================
 CHAUHAN ISMAILBHAI RASULBHAI  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: MR VAIBHAV N SHETH(5337) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR IMRAN H PATHAN(3478) for the Respondent(s) No. 2  MR. TIRTHRAJ PANDYA, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1

=
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI  Date : 10/07/2025  ORAL ORDER 1.

Learned advocates appearing for both parties jointly submitted that the complainant, who had earlier divorced the petitioner (her husband) under Muslim Personal Law, subsequently remarried him pursuant to the intervention of elderly members of the community.
It is further submitted that the FIR in question came to be registered during the intervening period between the divorce and the subsequent remarriage.

2. The complainant-victim is present before this Court and has voluntarily stated that she remarried the petitioner on her own volition on 09.04.2021, and that she is now residing with him peacefully.
It is further submitted that out of this wedlock, a girl child has been born, who is presently two years of age.

The complainant has also placed on record a copy of her second Nikahnama, the birth certificate of the minor child, and a duly NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/25066/2017 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined sworn settlement affidavit.

sentences.text: This Court has verified the willingness of the complainant- victim to proceed with the quashing of the FIR, and she has categorically affirmed that she has no objection to the same and that the dispute has been amicably resolved.
4. The petitioner, who was previously the complainant's ex- husband, has since remarried her, and they are now cohabiting harmoniously.

The matrimonial relationship, which had once deteriorated,
now stands reconciled and the parties are living together in peace and dignity.
5. In view of the above development, learned Additional Public Prosecutor Mr. Tirthraj Pandya has fairly submitted that this Court may pass appropriate orders in accordance with law.
6. It is pertinent to note that the FIR arises out of matrimonial discord, which has now been resolved amicably.
The complainant and the petitioner are presently living together and have a child born out of the present wedlock.

The complainant has filed a settlement affidavit on record, the relevant contents of which are reproduced hereinbelow:--
"I respectfully state that I am the original complainant and respondent no.2 in the captioned petition who has registered an FIR dated 16.05.2017 vide C. R. No. I - 47/2017 with Nandasan Police Station, Mehsana against the applicant herein,
wherein charge sheet is also laid by the investigation officer upon conclusion of investigation before the concerned court which is registered as Criminal Case No.
1101/2017 for the offences alleged to have been committed and punishable under sections 376 and 406 of IPC.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/25066/2017 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined

I respectfully say that the impugned FIR has been registered by me in complete hot haste and out of misunderstanding and on misconception of facts and with the intervention of elderly members of the family and trusted people of the community, the entire dispute is settled by and between me and the petitioner amicably and peacefully on my own free will and volition without any force, coercion or undue influence and we have remarried and happily reunited and staying as husband and wife together during the pendency of present quashing petition and thus, I withdraw all my allegations made by me in the FIR in question.
I further say that no dispute whatsoever remains or exists between me and the applicant and everything is settled between us peacefully and the grievance is amicably resolved.

I further say that in view thereof, I say that I have no objection and give my free consent for quashing of the impugned FIR and charge sheet filed therein and all other consequent proceedings arising therefrom by this Hon'ble Court and therefore,
the parties jointly request this Hon'ble Court to kindly be pleased to exercise the discretion in favour of the petitioner by quashing the criminal proceedings in the interest of justice taking into consideration the amicable settlement arrived at by and between the parties having reunited and leading a peaceful and happy married life together and the continuation of trial would be an exercise in futility and nothing but an harassment and humiliation."

sentences.text: The contents of the settlement affidavit have been verified with the complainant-victim in open Court, and she has duly affirmed and ratified the same.
She has unequivocally stated that she and the petitioner--who is now her husband--desire to continue their matrimonial relationship and reside together as a happily married couple.
8. The aforementioned developments are sufficient to bring the dispute between the parties to a quietus.

In such circumstances, continuation of the criminal proceedings against the petitioner, who is presently the lawfully wedded husband of the complainant- victim, would serve no fruitful purpose and would amount to an NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/25066/2017 ORDER DATED:
10/07/2025 undefined exercise in futility.
9. In the result, the application is allowed.

The impugned Criminal Complaint being C.R.-I No.47 of 2017 registered with Nandasan Police Station as well as all consequential proceedings initiated in pursuance thereof are hereby quashed and set aside.
Rule is made absolute.
Direct service is permitted.

(J. C. DOSHI,J) MANISH MISHRA Chauhan Ismailbhai Rasulbhai vs State Of Gujarat on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127608064/
